sharedLists.title: Shared Lists
sharedLists.markdownDescription:
Array of shared lists, which can be used in other plugins. Optional.

[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)

type.title: IP List
type.markdownDescription:
A list of IP addresses and CIDR ranges.

[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)

items.title: IP addresses and CIDR ranges
items.markdownDescription:
IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, plain or as CIDR ranges. Mixing both families in one list is allowed.

```json
{
  "type": "ipList",
  "items": ["1.1.1.1", "10.0.0.0/8", "2001:db8::1", "2001:db8::/32"]
}
```


[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)

type.title: AS List
type.markdownDescription:
A list of autonomous system numbers.

[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)

items.title: Autonomous system numbers
items.markdownDescription:
ASN numbers without the `AS` prefix, from 1 to 4294967295.

```json
{
  "type": "asList",
  "items": [13335, 15169, 32934]
}
```


[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.markdownDescription:
Please review documentation for this plugin before enabling it.

[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)

blockDuration.title: Block Duration
blockDuration.markdownDescription:
Duration of the block in seconds. 

 If the block duration is 0, the block will be permanent. 

 For example, if the block duration is 3600, the block will be permanent for 1 hour.

[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)

ip.title: IP
ip.markdownDescription:
List of IP addresses ranges to ignore from the block. 

 You can use lists from **sharedLists** in the format: **ext:list_name**. 

 You can also specify user IDs to ignore from the block. Please note that this field only supports IP addresses ranges, not CIDR ranges.

[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)

userId.title: User ID
userId.markdownDescription:
List of user IDs to ignore from the block. 

 You can also specify user IDs to ignore from the block.

[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)

ignoreLists.title: Ignore Lists
ignoreLists.markdownDescription:
List of IP addresses to ignore from the block. 

 You can use lists from **sharedLists** in the format: **ext:list_name**. 

 You can also specify user IDs to ignore from the block.

[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)

includeRuleTags.title: Include Rule Tags
includeRuleTags.markdownDescription:
By default, Torrent Blocker creates a dedicated rule and injects it as **routing.rules[0]**. Specify an array of **ruleTag** values here if you want to block IPs matched by other routing rules as well.

[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)

webhookUrl.title: Webhook URL
webhookUrl.markdownDescription:
Optional. Additional webhook URL to send to when a block is triggered.

[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)

rulePlacement.title: Rule Placement
rulePlacement.markdownDescription:
The position of the rule which Remnawave will inject into the routing.rules array. The default is 0. 

[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.markdownDescription:
If this plugin is enabled, all IP addresses specified in the **blockedIps** object will be blocked via nftables. **Use with caution.**

[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)

items.title: IP address or CIDR range
items.markdownDescription:
IP address or CIDR range. 

 You can use lists from **sharedLists** in the format: **ext:list_name**.

[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)

blockedIps.title: Blocked IPs
blockedIps.markdownDescription:
List of IP addresses and CIDR ranges to block via nftables. 

 You can use lists from **sharedLists** in the format: **ext:list_name**.

[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.markdownDescription:
If this plugin is enabled, outbound connections to specified IP addresses and ports will be blocked. **Use with caution.**

[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)

blockedIps.title: Blocked IPs
blockedIps.markdownDescription:
List of destination IP addresses and CIDR ranges to block. 

 You can use lists from **sharedLists** in the format: **ext:list_name**. 

 Example: `["10.0.0.1", "ext:blocked_destinations"]`

[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)

items.title: IP address or CIDR range
items.markdownDescription:
IP address or CIDR range. 

 You can use lists from **sharedLists** in the format: **ext:list_name**.

[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)

blockedPorts.title: Blocked Ports
blockedPorts.markdownDescription:
List of destination ports to block. 

 Example: `[25, 465, 587]` to block SMTP traffic.

[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.markdownDescription:
Controls whether IP addresses from the **whitelistIps** object will be used.

[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)

whitelistIps.title: Whitelist IPs
whitelistIps.markdownDescription:
List of IP addresses, for which the connection drop will not be applied, which is enabled by default for all IP addresses. 

 You can use lists from **sharedLists** in the format: **ext:list_name**. Please note that this field only supports IP addresses ranges, not CIDR ranges.

[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.markdownDescription:
Enables the pre-start stage. All enabled sections below run every time before the Xray-Core process starts — on node startup, on core restart, and after any configuration change that triggers a core reload. If a section fails, the failure is logged and the core still starts.

[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)

cleanupSockets.title: Cleanup Sockets
cleanupSockets.markdownDescription:
Stale unix socket removal before the core starts.

[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)

enabled.title: Enable socket cleanup
enabled.markdownDescription:
Removes stale unix socket files left behind by a previous core process that did not shut down cleanly. Such leftovers make Xray-Core fail to bind with `address already in use`. Only entries that are actually unix sockets are removed — regular files, directories and symlinks are always skipped.

[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)

files.title: Files
files.markdownDescription:
Absolute paths to socket files. Glob patterns are supported (`*`, `?`, `[…]`), for example `/dev/shm/*.sock`. Paths that do not exist are skipped silently.

[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.markdownDescription:
Enables the post-start stage. All enabled sections below run in the background every time the Xray-Core process has started and passed the health check - on node startup, on core restart, and after any configuration change that triggers a core reload.

[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)

webhook.title: Webhook
webhook.markdownDescription:
Webhook sent after the core starts.

[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)

enabled.title: Enable webhook
enabled.markdownDescription:
Sends a `POST` request with a JSON body to the URL once the core is up.

[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)

url.title: Webhook URL
url.markdownDescription:
URL to send the request to. 

 Body: `{ "scope": "service", "event": "service.core_started", "timestamp": "...", "metadata": { "name", "uuid", "id", "tags", "countryCode" } }`.

[📖 Documentation](https://docs.rw/docs/learn/node-plugins)
